newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish council warns TV on military coverage.
newsitem.headline: Turkish council warns TV on military coverage.

text.p: A Turkish broadcasting watchdog body warned television channels on Tuesday about their reporting of the military in a widening security scandal.
"Media organs must fulfil their legal obligations... Broadcasting must respect constitutional principles and democratic rules," the Radio and Television Supreme Council said in a statement.
The council, which has the authority to temporarily halt television broadcasts, said it was examining reports "covering some unfounded allegations and statements about the Turkish armed forces".

The media last week reported rumours that the military might intervene to clear up a scandal over alleged ties between officials and far-right gangsters. The influential armed forces have denied the charges.

The scandal erupted in November after a senior policeman and a gangster died in an accident in the same car. A government deputy who heads a militia that fights Kurdish rebels was injured in the crash.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition government last month threatened to clamp down on press criticism of state officials but a planned draft law restricting the media has yet to be debated in parliament.
